inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL prepared query combines SQL_SMALL_RESULT, an inner join, an OR range-or-pattern filter, a grouped MAX lookup in an IN subquery, CAST projection, and ordered LIMIT pagination.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored product-score page. Priority or label eligibility selects products, an inner score relation is restricted to each product's maximum score through a grouped IN subquery, CAST exposes a bounded label string, and stable label/score/metric ordering makes the page deterministic. Prepared statements, source tables, identifiers, values, and index churn are not copied.

fixture_notes: Products 101 and 103 qualify by priority, product 102 qualifies by the pro% label, and product 104 is excluded. The grouped MAX subquery keeps only each qualifying product's highest score; product 103 has a tied maximum, so the explicit metric ID tie-breaker makes LIMIT 3 deterministic.
determinism_notes: Product priorities, labels, scores, metric IDs, filter literals, and all ordering keys are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, prepared statements, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE catalog_products (product_id INT PRIMARY KEY, product_label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, priority INT NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE product_scores (metric_id INT PRIMARY KEY, product_id INT NOT NULL, score INT NOT NULL, score_note VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT SQL_SMALL_RESULT p.product_id, m.score, CAST(p.product_label AS CHAR(32)) AS label_text FROM catalog_products AS p INNER JOIN product_scores AS m ON m.product_id = p.product_id WHERE (p.priority BETWEEN 2 AND 4 OR p.product_label LIKE 'pro%') AND m.score IN (SELECT MAX(score) FROM product_scores GROUP BY product_id) ORDER BY p.product_label ASC, m.score DESC, m.metric_id ASC LIMIT 3

checks.sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_label, m.metric_id, m.score FROM catalog_products AS p INNER JOIN product_scores AS m ON m.product_id = p.product_id ORDER BY p.product_id, m.metric_id
